name: Johnny Storm

summary: Johnny and his older sister Sue grew up on Long Island until their mother, Mary, was killed in a car crash that their father, the surgeon Franklin Storm, could not save her from. Franklin fell into drinking and gambling and eventually went to prison for murder; rather than tell her brother the truth, Sue let him think their father was dead. The children were raised by their aunt Marygay in the town of Glenville, where Sue mothered her troublesome kid brother and Johnny, oddly enough given how his mother died, became obsessed with cars and turned into a skilled young mechanic.

At sixteen he followed Sue to Central City, California, where her fiancé Reed Richards was rushing to fly his experimental rocket before the government shut the project down. Reed's pilot, Ben Grimm, warned that the ship was not shielded well enough against radiation, but the four of them took it up anyway. Cosmic rays ripped through the cabin and forced a crash landing, and all four came back changed. Johnny found he could burst into flame and fly, and he took the name Human Torch from the android hero of World War II.

Reed convinced the group to use their new abilities for the public good as the Fantastic Four, and their first case sent them to Monster Isle to stop the Mole Man. Johnny was the youngest and most impatient of the four, forever needling Ben, and he spent his spare time finishing high school in Glenville while pretending to keep a secret identity. After one bust-up he walked out on the team, and while hiding in a run-down flophouse he recognised an amnesiac vagrant as the Sub-Mariner and jolted his memory back by dropping him into the sea, which set Namor on a war path against the surface world.

comics.title: Flame on
comics.summary: Johnny arrives as the hothead of the brand-new Fantastic Four, flaming on against the Mole Man's monsters in the team's first case. By the fourth issue he has quit in a sulk and, while hiding out, brings the long-lost Sub-Mariner back into the world. Later in 1962 he picks up a solo feature in Strange Tales, balancing hero work with small-town life in Glenville and unmasking a Soviet saboteur who calls himself the Destroyer.

comics.title: Crystal and the coming of Galactus
comics.summary: Johnny falls for Crystal, a young Inhuman with power over the elements, and is dragged away from her when Maximus traps her people inside the Great Refuge behind an unbreakable barrier. Soon afterwards the Silver Surfer leads Galactus to Earth, and the Watcher sends Johnny across space to the world-eater's ship to fetch the Ultimate Nullifier, the weapon Reed uses to make Galactus back off. Johnny then enrols at Metro College, where his roommate Wyatt Wingfoot becomes a close friend and joins his long hunt for a way back to Crystal.

comics.title: Frankie Raye
comics.summary: Crystal eventually leaves Johnny and marries Quicksilver, and after a few false starts he falls for Frankie Raye, a woman with a deep fear of fire. She discovers that her late stepfather, the inventor of the original android Human Torch, had accidentally given her flame powers and then hypnotised her into forgetting them. Johnny helps her learn to use them, but when a weakened Galactus needs a new herald, Frankie volunteers and leaves Earth as Nova, leaving him shattered.

comics.title: Secret Wars and Alicia
comics.summary: Pulled to the Beyonder's Battleworld, Johnny is healed by the alien Zsaji and loses her twice, first to Colossus and then to her own self-sacrifice. Back on Earth he grows close to Alicia Masters while Ben is still away, a romance that badly strains his friendship with the Thing. When a young fan dies after setting himself alight to imitate him, Johnny comes close to quitting as the Torch, but he carries on and marries Alicia.

comics.title: Lyja
comics.summary: Johnny learns that his wife is not Alicia at all but Lyja, a Skrull spy who had taken her place years earlier and then genuinely fallen for him. The team finds and frees the real Alicia, while Lyja seems to die shielding Johnny before being nursed back to health. When Skrull attackers corner him at Empire State University, his flame goes nova and burns down a large part of the campus, leaving him briefly a fugitive until Reed sells off patents to pay for the damage.

comics.title: Civil War and Secret Invasion
comics.summary: Angry at heroes after the Stamford disaster, a crowd outside a nightclub beats Johnny into a coma at the very start of the superhuman Civil War. When he wakes he goes with Sue to Captain America's underground Secret Avengers, the pair hiding under false identities as a married couple. During the Skrull invasion he, Ben and the Richards children are stranded in the Negative Zone by a Skrull posing as Sue, who turns out to be Lyja trying to keep them out of harm's way.

comics.title: Holding the door
comics.summary: When an endless insect army surges through the Negative Zone portal in the Baxter Building, Johnny throws Ben back through to Earth and stays on the far side so the door can be sealed. Annihilus kills him for refusing to open it, then has him revived and killed again and again. Johnny finally breaks out with other prisoners, takes Annihilus' Cosmic Control Rod and comes home at the head of an alien fleet, announcing himself by burning a giant 4 into the sky.

comics.title: A Torch without a family
comics.summary: When the multiverse ends, God Emperor Doom remakes Johnny as the sun hanging over his Battleworld. Reed rebuilds reality but leaves Johnny and Ben on Earth with altered memories, so both believe the rest of their family is dead and the Fantastic Four breaks up. Johnny works with the Inhumans, has a short romance with Medusa, joins the Avengers Unity Division, and later inherits Reed's patents, becoming a billionaire who buys Avengers Mansion.

comics.title: Spyre, Doom and a flame that will not go out
comics.summary: Ben takes Johnny on a trip across the multiverse to look for their family, and the full team is reunited soon after. A return to the planet Spyre gives Johnny a destined partner in the winged Sky, but he later cheats on her with Victorious, whom Doom plans to marry; when she confesses at the altar, Doom floods Johnny with concentrated cosmic rays so his flame can never switch off. He rallies Spyre's forces during the Reckoning War, then uses a Spyrian machine that reverses cosmic-ray mutations to get his normal powers back.

comics.title: Jonathan Fairweather
comics.summary: Reed sends the Baxter Building a year into the future to strand some invaders, but the children are still inside, and the furious team splits up. Unable to get hired under his own name, Johnny takes a store job as Jonathan Fairweather and helps his overworked coworkers bring down their boss, a former Maggia thug. The four make up, move into Aunt Petunia's old farmhouse in Benson, Arizona, and get the children back when the building returns.

screen.title: Fantastic Four
screen.summary: This Johnny is an astronaut on Victor von Doom's payroll, once Ben Grimm's subordinate, who pilots the space-station trip into the cosmic storm alongside his sister Sue. He loves his new powers from the start, sneaks off to a motocross event and hands the press the team's code names. In the final fight he dodges Doom's heat-seeking missile and helps superheat Doom so Reed and Ben can freeze him solid.

screen.title: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
screen.summary: Johnny chases the Silver Surfer, who hauls him into the thin upper atmosphere where his flame gutters out and then drops him. The encounter leaves his body in flux, so touching a teammate swaps their powers. In Shanghai he absorbs the abilities of the whole team at once and breaks Doom's hold on the Surfer's board.

screen.title: Fantastic Four
screen.summary: Here Johnny is Franklin Storm's son, a street racer who is put to work on his father's teleportation project after wrecking his car. He joins Reed, Victor and Ben on an unauthorised trip to Planet Zero, comes back wreathed in fire, and is trained by the government as a weapon in a suit that controls his flame. In the final battle he destroys the supports of Doom's energy construct, and the team then names itself the Fantastic Four.

screen.title: Deadpool & Wolverine
screen.summary: The MCU Wiki files this Johnny under the Void-Analyzing Fantastic Four Universe, while the Marvel Fandom wiki treats him as the Earth-121698 Johnny of the Fox films. Pruned by the TVA into the Void, he breaks up a fight between Deadpool and Wolverine, has his flame snuffed out by Pyro and is taken prisoner. When Deadpool repeats Johnny's crude insults to Cassandra Nova, she strips the skin from his body and kills him, and a tape in the closing credits shows he really did say them.

screen.title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
screen.summary: On Earth-828, Johnny is a former Eagle Scout and astronaut who chases the Silver Surfer into space and grabs her board before she shakes him off. He works through years of alien transmissions to crack her language, learns she is Shalla-Bal of Zenn-La, and uses what he finds to shake her loyalty to Galactus. In the battle for New York he tries to sacrifice himself to push Galactus through the last teleportation bridge, but Shalla-Bal shoves him aside and does it herself.

unverified: The 1994 Fantastic Four film (Jay Underwood as Johnny) is left out because it was never released. It was not researched further.
Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars appear on the MCU Wiki's Human Torch page as unreleased. Both are left out and no plot details were researched.

Avengers: Endgame Encore re-release (25 September 2026): the MCU Wiki's Endgame page lists the Encore-only cast and scenes, and Johnny Storm is not among them, so there is no entry. No other allowed source was checked.

Deadpool & Wolverine: the two wikis disagree on which universe the Void Johnny comes from (MCU Wiki: Void-Analyzing Fantastic Four Universe; Marvel Fandom wiki: Earth-121698, the Fox films). Both are reported. Neither wiki calls the role a cameo; it is marked cameo: true because he appears in one stretch of the film plus the credits tape.
Michael B. Jordan's Johnny shows up only as archive footage in the end credits of Deadpool & Wolverine (per the Marvel Fandom wiki's Earth-15866 page), so that is not listed as an appearance.

The versions of Johnny inside First Steps' in-universe TV show The Fantastic Four Power Hour (footage), the MCU Wiki's non-canon YouTube web series Meet the Fantastic Four (cast unconfirmed; not confirmed as live-action), and a variant mentioned only in a cancelled video game are all left out.
Later retcons shown on the Earth-616 page, such as a teenage run-in with the Amulet of Zarathos and Johnny training as a NASA pilot, are left out of the origin summary.
Frankie Raye era: the character page cites Fantastic Four #164 and #171 for the start of the romance; only #164 and #244 were checked on their issue pages.
Cover dates come from the Marvel Fandom issue pages; on-sale dates are earlier.
